answer: Sharing one crossing cannot stretch to a thousand identities, because weight rides on a single thread strung across one canyon span assigned to that identity alone. A velvet sleeve on the thread damps its vibration at a rate fixed by its fibre density, so auditors who pluck it and record resonance and decay get a signature no other span reproduces; a thread shared by two identities returns the same signature twice, and both lose weight. Fitting one span costs $80 once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 spans and sleeves, $80,000, each inspected in person, so no pool lends one crossing to many.
